result:
The simulator splits GPU time into kernels (alu/compute-class 17.3%, memory-latency 16.9%, HBM 15.7%), time inside all-reduces (30.9%), and idle gaps with no kernel or collective running (19.2%).

At batch 32, TP=8 leaves each GPU with tiny GEMMs and attention work. Eager launch adds gaps between the many small kernels. The 64 all-reduces per step are each only 256 KB, so they are latency-dominated. Communication is therefore the largest single share. The idle figure is the `idle_without_collectives` value, which excludes time inside collectives. The report's `gpu_idle_fraction` of 0.50 counts collective time too, so I didn't use it.

This is a simulation with a wide error band of about ±23% on step time, and the idle share is flagged as optimistic. The ranking is close: communication at 31% leads the 19% idle share by a clear margin. It leads the largest kernel class (compute, 17%) by about 14 points.
